title: Creation and validation of a questionnaire for eyelid surgery
summary:
Upper and lower eyelid corrections are common procedures that are both medically indicated due to pathologies or malpositions, as well as cosmetic procedures to achieve a more youthful and rejuvenated appearance.
However, the latter can lead to
eyelid malpositions that are both cosmetically unsatisfactory for the patient, or functional limitations and ultimately require further treatment.
The ageing of the periorbita is characterized by a number of processes that affect the aesthetics and function of the eyelids.
Some typical changes associated with the aging process are the loss of volume of the upper eyelid and periorbita, a higher position of the palpebral position of the eyelid crease, a lower position of the eyebrow, especially the lateral part, a reduction in skin
reduction in skin elasticity and dermatochalasis.
Dermatochalasis is a disease of the upper eyelid characterized by an excess of skin.
Dermatochalasis is often associated with selective visual field loss and a prolapse of the periorbital fat pads through the orbital septum. The nasal and central fat pads are located deep under the orbicularis muscle. Deep under
these fat pads is the levator palpebrae superioris muscle, which enters the nasal bone.

Patients with dermatochalasis and planned upper eyelid blepharoplasty, with ptosis and planned transcutaneous levator resection or with entropion/ectropion and planned tarsal reinplasty.
